items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: several members of the band were still living like, of course, Lil and Louie

ctx.x: So you researched the King Oliver chapter?

Partly. I wouldn't say that. Just the people in Chicago. Right. Because after all, Oliver did most of his important recording and you might say later playing in Chicago. So a lot of people there knew him and several members of the band were still living like, of course, Lil and Louie. And Bill Johnson, Dodds, both the Dodds brothers. So Ramsey couldn't get away from his job at Harcourt. So I did that work for him. All that we could. Unfortunately, no tape machines then. Just had to do it longhand. And I'd take…
Was Steve Smith's wife really interested and involved in things?

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-08-31
items.q: And he would work with Lil Armstrong and different people going up to Milwaukee and occasionally around Chicago.

ctx.x: Well, maybe you could correct him.

A footnote or something like that. Yes, sort of evaluate some of that, too. I'd rather do that and not take a lot of time on the tape now to do that. And they're not in a condition to be photostadded or Xerox or whatever it is. Another man who's dead now, Buddy Christian, an outstanding banjo and guitar player from New Orleans, who also played piano here and also in New York. And he played on quite a few of the Clarence Williams Hot Five. And what are they called? Blue Five, excuse me. Anyway, he's been dead for…
